items.title: List the GuardDuty detectors of two Regions
items.kills: "GuardDuty is a global service, so one switch covers every Region."
items.read_only_alternative: This task is read-only. It needs no alternative.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Ask AWS which Region your shell uses.
List the GuardDuty detectors in this Region.
steps.expect: "DetectorIds" with one detector ID if GuardDuty is on in this Region, or an empty list if it is off.

steps.text: Choose a second Region as <OTHER_REGION>, for example eu-west-1, or us-east-1 if your shell already uses eu-west-1. List the detectors there.
steps.expect: An empty list, or one detector ID that is not the ID from step 2.

items.title: Turn on GuardDuty without creating any logs
items.kills: "GuardDuty needs VPC Flow Logs and a CloudTrail trail that you turn on first."
items.cost: $0 in the 30-day free trial, which starts the first time an account uses GuardDuty in a Region. An account past its trial pays by the volume of logs and events that GuardDuty analyzes.
items.cost_if_forgotten: $0 a day while the free trial lasts. After the trial, the detector adds charges by the volume of logs and events that it analyzes.
items.read_only_alternative: Use this when GuardDuty is already on in the Region or you cannot create a detector. It changes nothing. Get the detector ID with aws guardduty list-detectors and use it as <DETECTOR_ID>. Read the data sources: aws guardduty get-detector --detector-id <DETECTOR_ID> --query "Features[].[Name,Status]" and compare them with aws ec2 describe-flow-logs --query "FlowLogs[].FlowLogId". FLOW_LOGS shows ENABLED even when the flow log list is empty. Then list the findings with aws guardduty list-findings --detector-id <DETECTOR_ID> and read one with aws guardduty get-findings --detector-id <DETECTOR_ID> --finding-ids <FINDING_ID>.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Check that GuardDuty is off in this Region. If the list shows a detector ID, stop and use the read-only alternative: the cleanup would delete that detector and its findings.
List the VPC flow logs in this Region. You create no flow log in this task.
steps.expect: A list of flow log IDs, often empty in a test account. Note the result.

steps.text: List the CloudTrail trails that this Region can see. You create no trail in this task.
steps.expect: A list of trail names, often empty in a test account.

steps.text: Turn on GuardDuty in this Region: create a detector with the two book tags. Keep its ID.
steps.expect: No output. DETECTOR_ID now holds the ID of the new detector.

steps.text: Read which data sources the new detector analyzes.
steps.expect: Pairs of a feature name and a status. FLOW_LOGS, CLOUD_TRAIL and DNS_LOGS show ENABLED. Some optional protection plans can also show ENABLED, because GuardDuty turns some of them on automatically.
steps.predict: You turned on no flow log and no trail for GuardDuty. Will FLOW_LOGS and CLOUD_TRAIL show ENABLED or DISABLED?
steps.explain: GuardDuty [pulls independent data streams directly](../facts/guardduty.md#guardduty-faq-no-need-to-enable-source-logs) from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS query logs. [You don't need to create or configure](../facts/guardduty.md#guardduty-flow-logs-not-required) VPC flow logs for GuardDuty to read flow log data. [GuardDuty does not manage or retain your logs](../facts/guardduty.md#guardduty-does-not-retain-logs): the data is [analyzed in near real time and discarded thereafter](../facts/guardduty.md#guardduty-does-not-retain-logs).

steps.text: No fix is needed: GuardDuty works without your logs. List the flow logs again to check that GuardDuty added none.
steps.expect: The same list as in step 2.

cleanup.text: Delete the detector. This turns GuardDuty off in this Region and deletes the findings of the detector.

verify.expect: An empty list. Then run aws guardduty list-detectors as well: DetectorIds shows an empty list. If it shows an ID, run the cleanup again.

still_costs: Nothing after the cleanup. A detector that stays on costs $0 a day during the free trial. After the trial, it adds charges by the volume of logs and events analyzed, also for the protection plans that are on.
GuardDuty can create the service-linked roles AWSServiceRoleForAmazonGuardDuty and AWSServiceRoleForAmazonGuardDutyMalwareProtection. They stay after the cleanup. IAM roles have no charge.
If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, DETECTOR_ID is empty. Find the ID again with aws guardduty list-detectors.
